text:
Sasha: Heads up — canary nodes in us-west2 are failing to finish boot after the 567.4 driver rollout. Kernel logs show a firmware signature check and GPU init race; nodes get stuck at GPU probe and never mark Ready.

infra-bot: Alert: 6 nodes in us-west2/canary failed healthcheck (nodepool-gpu-canary). See https://fleet.internal/alerts/ALRT-2026-321.

Ben: Copy. Can you paste the last 20 lines of dmesg from one of the affected hosts? Any DKMS compile errors?

Sasha: Grabbed one. Shortened: 
```
[    3.412345] nvidia: probe of 0000:65:00.0 failed with error -22
[    3.412350] nvidia: fw_sig_check: firmware signature verification failed for nvidia/pmu_fw.bin
[    3.412352] nvidia: GPU init timed out: nv_init_wait failed
[    3.412360] kernel: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing - tainting kernel
```

Kai: Hmm, that looks like the new firmware blobs that ship with 567.4 have a signature that doesn't match the kmod signing key we use in our AMIs. DKMS does try to build the module but the kernel refuses to load an unsigned module if secureboot/module-signing is enforced. Any DKMS build logs?

Sasha: DKMS log snippet attached to the node (pasted): 
```
DKMS: build start for nvidia-567.4 for kernel 6.4.18
make: Entering directory '/usr/src/nvidia-567.4'
gcc ... -D__KERNEL__ ... -o nvidia.ko
Error! Bad return status for module build on kernel: 6.4.18
Consult /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/567.4/build/make.log for more information.
make: *** [modules] Error 2
```

Maria: We also saw one eu-west2 canary node flare up with the same fw_sig_check message earlier this morning, but it recovered after reinstalling the older driver package. Not sure if it's broadly correlated with kernel minor versions (6.4.x vs 6.5.x).

Ben: Immediate action: hold the rollout (stop canary -> prod promotion). Kai, can you prepare an emergency rollback to 560.102 for the canary pool and verify boot? If rollback fixes boot, we'll pause the rollout and open a kernel/firmware compatibility task.

Kai: On it. Rolling back canary now — plan: 
1) cordon and drain nodes in nodepool-gpu-canary (safe-drain).
2) replace package nvidia-driver=567.4 -> 560.102 via apt/yum artifact repo.
3) reboot and watch kubelet + GPU plugin.

ops-rotation: Noted — this may temporarily reduce available GPU capacity in us-west2. If rollback reduces available nodes below 50% of expected, we should autoscale extra spot-backed instances to keep CI and training jobs alive. Cost impact estimate: +~$2.1k/day if we spin up 8 replacement nodes in on-demand while we stabilize.

Kai: Replaced driver on 3/6 canary nodes, one recovered cleanly and rejoined. Two still showing DKMS build failure — digging into their kernel package diffs (one had a vendor-patched kernel with module-signing stricter flags).

Ben: Please collect the following and drop into the incident doc: kernel version, kernel config snippet (CONFIG_MODULE_SIG=y, CONFIG_IMA=y, CONFIG_MODULE_SIG_HASH=...), dkms version, and exact nvidia package checksums. Also check nvlink firmware versions with: 
```
strings /lib/firmware/nvidia/pmu_fw.bin | head -n 5
sha256sum /usr/lib/nvidia/567.4/*.ko
```

Sasha: Will do. Quick question — do we want to temporarily disable module signature enforcement on those nodes as a mitigation? That's risky for compliance.

Maria: I'd avoid disabling signature enforcement in prod. For canary it's less risky but still not great. Prefer rollback + deeper fix (re-sign modules with our key or update AMI signing keys so kernel trusts the new signatures).

Kai: Agree. Early hypothesis: vendor changed signing key for pmu blobs or switched to new key rotation. Two remediation paths: 1) repackage 567.4 modules signed with our CI key (fast, manual), or 2) update bootloader/AMI keyring to accept vendor key (longer, more secure). We'll start with path 1 for canary recovery while we track path 2 for a proper rollout.

Ben: Assigning follow-ups: Sasha — gather dmesg + /var/lib/dkms logs from all affected nodes (due in 30m). Kai — rollback and validate 1h runway. Maria — coordinate with security on signing plan. ops-rotation — monitor capacity and estimate cost if we need to scale.

infra-bot: Incident doc created: https://incidents.internal/RWF-2026-067 (priority P2) — responders: Sasha, Kai, Maria.

Sasha: Uploaded collected artifacts to the incident doc. Noted a pattern: nodes with custom vendor kernels (kernel-rt or vendor-patch) are more likely to fail.

Ben: Good catch. That suggests we need a preflight matrix for driver rollouts that includes kernel flavor checks. Add that to the rollout checklist: 
- allowed kernel versions/flavors
- module-signing key check (verify vendor sig matches org keyring or modules are resignable)
- firmware checksum/expected hash

Kai: I'll add the checklist and block future rollouts until we have an automated preflight in CI. For now, holding at canary and rolling back prod push.

Maria: FYI — Security already pinged vendor about the signing change. They acknowledged a key rotation last week but assumed backwards compatibility. We're awaiting details.

ops-rotation: Scaling up 4 spot-backed nodes in us-west2 as a precaution; will cancel if rollback brings adequate capacity.

Sasha: Thanks all — continuing artifact collection and will post final status in 45m. :thumbsup:
